blocks.text: A blood group system classifies blood by the presence of particular antigens on the red blood cells (RBCs). The International Society of Blood Transfusion recognizes 43 blood group systems in humans, and each system has its own blood groups.

The most important is the ABO system (groups A, B, AB and O), and the second is the Rh system (Rh-positive and Rh-negative). For a blood transfusion the ABO and Rh groups of donor and recipient must match.

blocks.title: For information
blocks.text: The antigens on the surface of red cells that define blood groups may be proteins, carbohydrates, glycoproteins or glycolipids.
